note: Conditions are generated from `factors` x `design`, so the experiment is written down once instead of as N hand-copied command templates. A cell is named `<chain>-<resolution>-<model>[-i<D>]`: architecture, source resolution, model variant and (when above 1) frames in flight -- and nothing else. The seven-op conditioning chain is a *constant* of the experiment (`conditioning` below), not a coordinate: every cell, monolith and ROS 2, at every shape, runs it, and `run.py` rejects a cell whose command disagrees. `--conditions` selects a subset by cell name; `cells` overrides per-cell knobs. If `factors` is absent the older flat `conditions` block is used instead.

conditioning.note: The one stage-2 chain, in canonical order, run by every cell. It is declared here so there is a single source of truth for it: the ROS templates splice `{pre_ops}` into `pre_ops:=`, the monolith template spells the same list as repeated `--pre`, and `run.py` checks both forms against `ops` before launching -- a cell that skipped it would otherwise look faster, because `pre_ms` is a sum and identity is free. Measured cost of the chain on the monolith: 103.5 ms/frame at 720p and 13.6 at 180p; 360p (~31.6) is interpolated in pixels between them (chain-shapes.md, 200-frame calibration). Do not add a cell that runs a subset: that is a different experiment, and the records cannot tell them apart.

anchor_note: The reference cell every delta is expressed against. Not measured more often than the other cells -- every cell runs once per pass -- so its job is to be the shared zero: any run of a subset of the matrix must include it, or that run yields no comparable delta. It is the headline cell and the anchor of the historic baseline; it is no longer the cheapest cell (the conditioning chain costs ~103.5 ms at 720p against ~13.6 at 180p), but `analyze.py --anchor` re-derives every delta from the records already on disk, so changing it costs nothing.

trial.note: The design is stated in frames -- that is what the percentiles are computed from -- and each trial gets a time ceiling derived from them, because the machine state that dominates trial-to-trial variance is a function of elapsed time, not of frame count. `settle_s` is skipped by the analyser (thermal/clock ramp); `analysis_frames` is then taken verbatim, so every cell reports percentiles over the same n. `fps_hint` is a table of estimates per (chain, resolution, model) and must be PESSIMISTIC: each value is ~0.7x the expected rate with the seven-op chain, which costs ~103.5 ms/frame at 720p and ~13.6 at 180p on top of the op-free pipeline (59.5 fps for monolith-720p-n before conditioning). It is per resolution and model, not one scale on a 720p row, because the ops and the model scale differently with pixels: at 720p the chain is ~7x the inference of the n engine, at 180p they are comparable, so the model spread widens as the resolution falls. An over-estimate shortens the ceiling until the window goes short; an under-estimate only runs a little longer. Re-derive from a clean run and keep the margin.

resolution.note: Three re-encodes of the same clip at the same CRF, so bitrate (and therefore decode cost) scales with resolution. They are stored upright: ffmpeg baked the rotation into the pixels and cleared the display matrix, hence rotate 0. `clip_frames` is what makes the replay count exact instead of a 1000-loop fudge. With the conditioning chain in every cell, resolution no longer moves only the payload: the ops cost 103.5 ms/frame at 720p and 13.6 at 180p, so the per-frame cost of every cell changes by ~7x along this axis. That is why `trial.fps_hint` is a per-(chain, resolution, model) table rather than a 720p row with one scale.

model.note: All three engines take FLOAT (1,3,640,640) and produce FLOAT (1,84,8400), so the model axis moves zero bytes on the wire and only the engine's own cost changes. imgsz is not a launch parameter any more (the inference node reads the contract off the engine), and the wire no longer carries a tensor at all: both hops out of stage 2 carry the BGR frame, so transport scales with source resolution instead of paying a fixed 4.9 MB per frame.

ros-N2-p1c0.note: two processes: acquisition | everything else. One pixel hop and nothing else, so this cell prices a process boundary -- if a ROS cost exists that is not transport, it appears here first. p1c0, N2.
ros-N2-p1c0.shell: source {repo}/ws/install/setup.bash && PYTHONPATH={repo}/monolith/yolocar/src:$PYTHONPATH ros2 launch yolocar_ros bench.launch.py model:={model} max_frames:={frames} duration:={duration} loops:={loops} source:={source} rotate:={rotate} 'chain:=acq|pre+infer+post' 'pre_ops:={pre_ops}' inflight:={inflight} records:={out}/records.jsonl summary:={out}/summary.json log_level:=WARNING

ros-N3-p1c1.note: pixels cross one boundary: three processes but only one frame serialisation. It beats p2c0 despite the same node count if H1 holds. p1c1, N3.
ros-N3-p1c1.shell: source {repo}/ws/install/setup.bash && PYTHONPATH={repo}/monolith/yolocar/src:$PYTHONPATH ros2 launch yolocar_ros bench.launch.py model:={model} max_frames:={frames} duration:={duration} loops:={loops} source:={source} rotate:={rotate} 'chain:=acq|pre+infer|post' 'pre_ops:={pre_ops}' inflight:={inflight} records:={out}/records.jsonl summary:={out}/summary.json log_level:=WARNING

ros-N3-p2c0.note: the mirror of p1c1: same process count, pixels cross twice. p1c1 vs p2c0 is the H1 test -- same N, different payload classes. p2c0, N3.
ros-N3-p2c0.shell: source {repo}/ws/install/setup.bash && PYTHONPATH={repo}/monolith/yolocar/src:$PYTHONPATH ros2 launch yolocar_ros bench.launch.py model:={model} max_frames:={frames} duration:={duration} loops:={loops} source:={source} rotate:={rotate} 'chain:=acq|pre|infer+post' 'pre_ops:={pre_ops}' inflight:={inflight} records:={out}/records.jsonl summary:={out}/summary.json log_level:=WARNING

ros-N4-p2c1.note: four-node chain (acquisition -> preprocessing -> inference -> postprocessing), one process each, running the seven-op conditioning chain like every other cell. The inference node owns the decode/threshold step, so compare `infer + post` against the monolith's two buckets. This is the only cell both the model matrix and the shape axis need: it is p2c1 with the common workload, so the shape axis gets its four-node baseline without a second cell. Prerequisite: `cd ws && colcon build --symlink-install`.
ros-N4-p2c1.shell: source {repo}/ws/install/setup.bash && PYTHONPATH={repo}/monolith/yolocar/src:$PYTHONPATH ros2 launch yolocar_ros bench.launch.py model:={model} max_frames:={frames} duration:={duration} loops:={loops} source:={source} rotate:={rotate} 'chain:=acq|pre|infer|post' 'pre_ops:={pre_ops}' inflight:={inflight} records:={out}/records.jsonl summary:={out}/summary.json log_level:=WARNING

ros-N5-p3c1.note: one pixel hop more than p2c1 and nothing else: the additivity check. Its delta against p2c1 must reproduce one hop cost, or the per-hop model is wrong. p3c1, N5.
ros-N5-p3c1.shell: source {repo}/ws/install/setup.bash && PYTHONPATH={repo}/monolith/yolocar/src:$PYTHONPATH ros2 launch yolocar_ros bench.launch.py model:={model} max_frames:={frames} duration:={duration} loops:={loops} source:={source} rotate:={rotate} 'chain:=acq|pre|pre|infer|post' 'pre_ops:={pre_ops}' pre_groups:=2,5 inflight:={inflight} records:={out}/records.jsonl summary:={out}/summary.json log_level:=WARNING

ros-N5-p2c2.note: first cut inside stages 4-6: nms alone, then filter+coord. Candidate hops carry kilobytes, so this is the cheapest boundary in the pipeline. p2c2, N5.
ros-N5-p2c2.shell: source {repo}/ws/install/setup.bash && PYTHONPATH={repo}/monolith/yolocar/src:$PYTHONPATH ros2 launch yolocar_ros bench.launch.py model:={model} max_frames:={frames} duration:={duration} loops:={loops} source:={source} rotate:={rotate} 'chain:=acq|pre|infer|nms|filter+coord' 'pre_ops:={pre_ops}' inflight:={inflight} records:={out}/records.jsonl summary:={out}/summary.json log_level:=WARNING

ros-N6-p2c3.note: stages 4-6 fully split: three candidate hops. With p2c2 it gives the marginal cost of a candidate boundary. p2c3, N6.
ros-N6-p2c3.shell: source {repo}/ws/install/setup.bash && PYTHONPATH={repo}/monolith/yolocar/src:$PYTHONPATH ros2 launch yolocar_ros bench.launch.py model:={model} max_frames:={frames} duration:={duration} loops:={loops} source:={source} rotate:={rotate} 'chain:=acq|pre|infer|nms|filter|coord' 'pre_ops:={pre_ops}' inflight:={inflight} records:={out}/records.jsonl summary:={out}/summary.json log_level:=WARNING

ros-N12-p8c3.note: the far end: one process per op plus split stages 4-6. Eleven hops, eight of them carrying a frame -- the transport-dominant extreme of the axis. p8c3, N12.
ros-N12-p8c3.shell: source {repo}/ws/install/setup.bash && PYTHONPATH={repo}/monolith/yolocar/src:$PYTHONPATH ros2 launch yolocar_ros bench.launch.py model:={model} max_frames:={frames} duration:={duration} loops:={loops} source:={source} rotate:={rotate} 'chain:=acq|pre|pre|pre|pre|pre|pre|pre|infer|nms|filter|coord' 'pre_ops:={pre_ops}' pre_groups:=1,1,1,1,1,1,1 inflight:={inflight} records:={out}/records.jsonl summary:={out}/summary.json log_level:=WARNING

design.note: Architecture x resolution x model, plus the frames-in-flight ladder: 40 cells. It is listed in full so the file states the truth rather than a wish; `bench/README.md` has the cost per cell and the pruning recipes (`--conditions`, or a shorter `design`). The model matrix is 2 chains x 3 resolutions x 3 models = 18; `ros-N4-p2c1` is also the four-node baseline of the shape axis, so it is not listed twice. The shape cells (`ros-N*`, 14 more) run two resolutions and model n as their own subset; the eight fourth-coordinate cells are the frames-in-flight ladder (window 2, 4 or 8 instead of 1), which only exists for the ROS chains -- the monolith is one thread, so its window is 1 by construction. Run a ladder as its own `--conditions` subset with its `i1` cell of the same family in the same invocation: that cell is the local zero for every window delta, while `anchor` stays the monolith.

artifacts.note: Demo material, NOT measurement: `bench/run.py --demo` runs each condition once through one full replay of the clip with the detections sidecar on, then renders it offline with `yolocar.demo`. Nothing here touches the measured trials, so the measured commands above stay byte-identical.

monolith-ctrl.note: Same as `monolith`: two visually identical control videos are the noise floor, made visible.

run.shell: source {repo}/ws/install/setup.bash && PYTHONPATH={repo}/monolith/yolocar/src:$PYTHONPATH ros2 launch yolocar_ros bench.launch.py loops:={loops} duration:=-1 source:={source} rotate:={rotate} 'chain:=acq|pre|infer|post' 'pre_ops:={pre_ops}' records:={out}/records.jsonl detections:={out}/detections.jsonl summary:={out}/summary.json log_level:=WARNING

compare.note: Side-by-side, each panel at its own pace (`--align wall`): the ROS panel stutters and the composite lasts as long as the slower run.

order.note: `auto` keeps the cyclic Latin square where it is cheap and correct (<= 6 cells, repeats a multiple of the cell count), and otherwise shuffles blocks per pass with a logged seed and reverses the direction inside a block on alternate passes. `block_by` groups the cells that should be measured back-to-back: here a monolith and a ROS cell at the same resolution and model, so a chain delta is a difference of minutes, not hours. Blocks are grouped by factors rather than by cell name so editing `design` cannot silently desynchronise them.

cells.note: Per-cell overrides, merged over the generated cell. The `ros-N*` shape cells set `fps_hint` explicitly: their cost is dominated by the conditioning chain and the partition, which the matrix table (indexed by chain, resolution and model) does not cover. `ros-N4-p2c1` itself needs no override: it is a matrix cell, so `trial.fps_hint` covers it. Use this block for a measured hint, a different window for one cell, or "enabled": false to retire a cell. The window cells (`-iD`) also set `settle_s: 45`: a 4 fps cell and a 40 fps cell are different power and thermal states on the same board, so the ramp takes longer than the 30 s the rest of the matrix uses. Their `fps_hint` is the *expected* peak at that window with the usual margin taken off (the closed-loop prediction is `X = min(D / sum(residency), 1 / max residency)`), and an over-estimate only costs a `window_short` warning. With the conditioning chain the montage is asymmetric: at 720p the pre node costs ~103.5 ms and becomes the bottleneck, so the window buys little beyond two frames; at 180p the ops are ~13.6 ms and the model still sets the pace. These hints are estimates, so lower them on a loaded board.
